title: Deck Staining in Hawthorne, FL | Strip, Sand & Seal
description: Deck staining in Hawthorne, FL for shaded, damp lake-country decks: strip, sand, replace bad boards, and apply penetrating stain that is back-brushed in.
heroIntro: A deck under live oaks near the lakes rarely dries out completely between summer storms. We restore it with a strip-and-sand prep and a penetrating stain chosen for that kind of exposure.

sections.h2: Why decks around Hawthorne wear out the way they do
body: Hawthorne's lake-side lots tend to be shady and green, which is pleasant for sitting outside and hard on wood. Boards under tree cover stay damp for days after a summer storm, collect leaf tannin stains, and grow mildew in the grooves. The sunny ends of the same deck go gray and splinter from UV. Deck staining in Hawthorne, FL has to deal with both conditions on one surface. It is a regular request across our Hawthorne service area.
Soft spots and dark, spongy board ends are signs of rot underneath. Our article on signs of deck wood rot shows what to check before you call.

sections.h2: Prep is most of the job
body: Stain only performs on bare, open wood. We strip failed coatings, clean off mildew and tannin, and sand the deck flat so the new stain soaks in evenly instead of sitting on top. Damaged boards and loose fasteners are replaced or reset before any finish goes on. Stain is sprayed and then back-brushed into the grain, which pushes product into checks and end grain where water does its damage.

bullets: Transparent: shows the most grain, needs the most frequent recoats
Semi-transparent: a balance of grain and UV protection, our most common pick
Solid: hides mismatched or patched boards and lasts longest on the surface, but can wear in traffic lanes
body: On a deck that mixes old and new boards after repairs, a semi-transparent or solid tone helps everything read as one surface. We will show you samples on your own wood before committing.

sections.h2: Keeping the new finish looking good
body: A little upkeep stretches the time between full restorations. Sweep leaves off before they sit and stain, keep planters on feet so water does not pool under them, and rinse pollen off in spring. When the traffic lanes begin to look lighter than the edges, a maintenance coat on clean wood is far less work than stripping a deck that has been left to fail.

sections.h2: Scheduling and what else gets stained
body: Stain needs dry wood and a dry forecast, so deck work fits best into the October-to-May stretch, with summer jobs started early in the day. Railings, stairs, and pergolas can be included. If the deck connects to a fence line, our Hawthorne fence painting and staining can be done in the same visit, and we often start with a gentle wash of the surrounding siding. For product details see our deck and fence staining service.

faqs.q: How often does a Hawthorne deck need re-staining?
faqs.a: It depends on shade, opacity, and foot traffic. Shady, damp decks and transparent stains need attention sooner. We will look at yours and tell you what to expect.

faqs.q: Can you save a gray, weathered deck?
faqs.a: Usually. Gray wood is surface UV damage that sanding removes. Boards that are soft or rotted are replaced instead.

faqs.q: Do you paint decks instead of staining them?
faqs.a: We generally recommend penetrating stain on walking surfaces because paint film peels under foot traffic and standing water. Solid stain gives a painted look with less peeling.
